items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: The interviewee does not speak in the provided context. The mention of Kenny Dorham is made by the Interviewer describing a past event ('Charlie Parker, Kenny Dorham, and it was a great band... Dorham blowing them away man'). ctx.x: And like to the bebop. Even the bebop era, they had a special dance that they did. I mean not just a special dance, but it was a concept, and they improvised out there.

In the late ‘40s in Buffalo, there was a place on the east side called Amity Hall and there was a big poster out front, “Charlie Parker Quintet.” And it was a dance hall. And it was Charlie Parker, Kenny Dorham, and it was a great band. And they were playing, and people were dancing, I mean it was a dance. We were standing in the corner listening, people were listening, people were dancing. And I thought that was pretty healthy, at the time, you know I’m not a dancer you know so I don’t know exactly what people…
Well it does seem kind of odd sometimes to be listening to say the Count Basie Orchestra in the concert hall, and they’re just swinging and swinging. People almost should be dancing to this music.
